name: Mute & Co
blurb: Brand identity for sound-first products — labels, headphones, streaming apps. Quiet typography, strong silhouettes. Known for letting negative space do the talking.

name: Folio Dept
blurb: Editorial-first branding for publishers, zines, and literary brands. Masters of type hierarchy and the kind of cover that makes someone pick up a book off a shelf.

name: Verde Studio
blurb: Sustainability and outdoor brands. Their work puts you in the field — texture, topographic detail, earthy restraint. Clients are B-corps, trail gear, and regenerative food.

name: Slab
blurb: Brutalist brand identities for fashion, architecture, and nightlife. Thick rules, raw grids, type that hits you before you've read it. Not for the faint of heart.

name: Kuroi
blurb: Japanese-influenced branding for wellness, skincare, and hospitality. Japandi sensibility — restraint, ritual, natural materials, zero wasted elements.

name: Flux Form
blurb: Neo-futurist tech and SaaS brands. They understand that B2B doesn't have to be boring — dark-mode-first, motion-ready systems that work in pitch decks and dashboards.

name: Palate Works
blurb: Food, beverage, and hospitality identities that make you hungry. Warm but never saccharine — tactile packaging, hand-drawn elements, and type you'd find on a 1970s diner menu.

name: Seam Studio
blurb: Luxury and accessible fashion brands — from haute streetwear to sustainable sportswear. Systems thinkers who design for print, label, tag, and social in one pass.

name: Helix & Co
blurb: Sports, fitness, and performance brands. High-energy visual systems that translate from stadium billboards to app icons. They have an in-house motion team.

name: Alcove
blurb: Home goods, interiors, and lifestyle brands. Art-deco revival meets Scandinavian restraint. Their packaging feels like an object before you've even opened it.
